newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo head ups 1996 sales forecast.
newsitem.headline: Valeo head ups 1996 sales forecast.

text.p: French car parts maker Valeo expects to post 29 billion francs in sales for 1996, slightly higher than the 28.5 billion initially estimated, chairman Noel Goutard said on Tuesday.

"After the first nine months in which the group announced a 16.7 percent increase in turnover, we think we will be close to 29 billion francs for the 1996 year," he told a news conference. Valeo made 1995 sales of 25.23 billion francs.
French holding group CGIP earlier said it is buying 20 percent of Valeo for 4.68 billion francs from Cerus, owned by Italian businessman Carlo De Benedetti.
Goutard added that Valeo's 40-billion-franc sales target set for 2000 was now viewed as a "minimum objective."
Valeo's new ownership will allow it to go to the capital markets for cash to fund acquisitions, which was not possible before as Cerus did not want to dilute its holding, he said.
"The new capital configuration will favour Valeo's development, which will now be able to go to the markets to fund its expansion," he said.

Access to the markets would also allow Valeo to pursue a more generous dividend policy, he added. "We were in the situation where we could only finance growth from own-resources. Our dividend policy had to take account of that need to be self-financing," he said.
"With the possibility of gaining access to the capital markets, we will be able to pursue a more open dividend policy," he said.
Valeo's board on Monday agreed to pay an exceptional 10 franc dividend on November 18.

CGIP chairman Ernest-Antoine Seilliere earlier said he expected Valeo to pay about a third of net profits in dividends, in contrast to the 15-18 percent it historically paid. He also said he wanted Valeo to be more active in acquiring companies and to increase debt to leverage its financial results.

Cerus is selling its 20 percent in Valeo to CGIP, while the state-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) is raising its Valeo stake to 5.4 percent from 1.9 and the JP Morgan GT Corporation fund is taking 3.6 percent.
